A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DisPose and provide readable text, equations, tables, figures and appendices A–H. The complete material supports reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered illustrations.

before.justification: v1 reports original DisPose evaluations on TikTok and an unseen dataset, qualitative generation results, component and architecture ablations, and image-quality and efficiency measurements.

after.justification: v3 retains the original quantitative evaluations in Tables 1–7 and qualitative experiments throughout the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Figure 2 retain the same sparse/dense motion guidance, CMP propagation, DIFT keypoint correspondence and hybrid ControlNet. No algorithmic, architectural, objective or inference-procedure revision is described.

E1.justification: Both versions document internet human-video training data, TikTok evaluation and the 30-video unseen dataset with generated reference images. Cross-identity, multi-view and background-condition examples are also retained; no new coverage appears.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain MagicPose, Moore-AnimateAnyone, MusePose, ControlNeXt and MimicMotion. Champ remains the qualitative dense-guidance comparator, and the appendix comparisons retain their comparator sets.

E3.justification: Section 5.1 changes the reported MimicMotion-side hybrid-ControlNet initialization from stable-video-diffusion-img2vid-xt-1-1 to stable-video-diffusion-img2vid-xt. Other stated training budgets, resolutions, frame counts, splits and metrics remain unchanged. This is a reported setting revision; the PDFs do not establish whether it reflects a correction or rerun.

E4.justification: Both retain motion/point, hybrid-ControlNet and CMP ablations, plus semantic-correspondence, cross-identity, multi-view, training/inference flow and background-noise analyses. The appendix visualizations are relocated or renumbered without adding or removing analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, error bars, confidence intervals or formal significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice is added.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 retain their numerical results, and the qualitative illustrations match. Table 7's 653.4 becomes 653.40, an equivalent representation. Table 6 corrects metric-direction labels while retaining its scores and accompanying performance conclusion.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 retain the same diffusion, motion-field, correspondence and control-residual definitions. No mathematical assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions and conclusion retain the same claims: disentangled pose guidance without additional dense inputs, plug-and-play integration with frozen animation models, and improved generation quality and generalizability.

C2.justification: Interpretations of dense-guidance shape constraints, component benefits and training/inference flow differences are retained. Limitations concerning unseen body regions, background noise and inference cost remain unchanged in Section 7 and Appendices D, G and H.

D1.justification: Section 5.1 revises both the SVD initialization identifier and its model-source link, changing the checkpoint specified for reproduction. Other implementation details, watershed sampling instructions and the DisPose repository address remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds eight cited works, including Ma et al. (2017, 2018), Jin et al. (2024) and Zeng et al. (2024), and removes VideoSwap (Gu et al., 2024). Section 4.1 also drops the explicit Gaussian-filtering inspiration attribution to Yin et al. and Wang et al. The central research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 adds an ICLR 2025 header, a corresponding-author note and acknowledgements, alongside local wording and terminology edits. Examples include Control Guidance becoming Pose Guidance and Code becoming Project page. The main narrative and appendix section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: Several existing figures and tables are relocated while retaining their designs and content. The background-noise illustration moves from v1 Figure 15 to v3 Figure 13 beside Appendix H. Table 6 corrects the arrows to SSIM/PSNR higher-is-better and LPIPS/L1 lower-is-better.

improvement.justification: Correcting Table 6's reversed metric-direction arrows removes a misleading contradiction with its unchanged values and Appendix F's conclusion. Bringing the background-noise illustration alongside its discussion also improves readability. These are limited gains: the empirical evidence remains unchanged, and the checkpoint revision is not explained as a correction or rerun.
